a1.say: Let's solve Odd Positions, Then Even Positions, using the Two Pointers (odd and even chains) approach.

a1.cap: Regroup the list so all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd, …) come first, followed by the nodes at even positions, keeping the relative order within each group. Use O(1) extra space and return the head.
a1.say: Regroup the list so all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd,... ) come first, followed by the nodes at even positions, keeping the relative order within each group. Use O of one extra space and return the head.

lines: Regroup the list so all nodes at odd positions (1st, 3rd, …) come first, followed by the nodes at even positions, keeping the relative order within each group. Use O(1) extra space and return the head.

a1.cap: For example, with head = [1,2,3,4,5], the answer is [1,3,5,2,4].
a1.say: For example, with head equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the answer is 1, 3, 5, 2, 4.

a1.cap: Keep two chains: odd starts at the first node and even at the second. Repeatedly link each to the node after the other, which leapfrogs them forward.
Finally connect the end of the odd chain to the head of the even chain.
Let's walk through it with head = [1,2,3,4,5].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with head equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

a1.cap: The even chain grows to the end.
Attach the even chain after the last odd node.
Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Two Pointers (odd & even chains) approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
